line2: A corpus this film can count, and you cannot yet clone.
narration: The method behind this laboratory is written down. Not as a paper, but as an encyclopedia and a cookbook — chapters, recipes and a lexicon, in a repository of their own. The next frames count it, quote it, and then say plainly what stands between that corpus and you.

asks: How large is the written corpus, and what counted it?
source: lab/film/welcome/qc/tokens.cjs — the corpus figures are directory walks and a lexicon read, evaluated when the frame is built
note: Chapters are markdown files counted on disk. Concepts and domains are read out of the lexicon's own file.
narration: @n.corpus.chapters chapters. @n.corpus.concepts concepts in the lexicon, across @n.corpus.domains registered domains. Not one of those figures is typed into this film. On screen is the tail of the run that resolved every number you will hear: its first three lines are corpus counts, and its last is how many figures the register resolved without failing.

why: What the first chapter of the cookbook says it is building
narration: This is how the corpus opens. Not with a result, but with the kitchen: the governance discipline, the pantry, and the fence vocabulary that binds every recipe. Read this before you cook anything. Under the frame is the file, the line range, and a digest recomputed from those bytes as the frame was made.

runs: git ls-files | grep -ciE "licen[cs]e|copying"; grep -m1 "^## STATUS" deploy/PUBLISH-DECISION.md
prints_literal:
0
## STATUS: STAGED, NOT DEPLOYED. NOTHING IS EXPOSED.
asks: Can you take this corpus home today?
source: run at the root of the UNI-Encyclopedia-Cookbook repository — a count of tracked licence files, then the corpus's own exposure decision
note: No licence file yet. That the repository is not public is stated by the operator, not counted by this frame.
narration: The mission clause says free and open. Here is where the corpus stands against it today. Zero files tracked in that repository match a licence or a copying notice, and its own exposure document opens with the words on screen. It is not public, and that part is the operator's statement rather than something this frame counts.
